docs.presetsSurfaces.component: The looks the kit already has, registered under a name: `plate`, `bare`, `zone`, `ink`, `mark`
and `trail`. See `presets/surfaces.ts` for the numbers each one holds.
This is NOT the page to rebuild a record from its parts — that whole panel, every field a
`SurfaceRecord` can carry, already lives on `Atoms/Surfaced → Plate`. What this shelf answers
is a different question: "what does this NAME already look like", so the only control on each
page is the box or run it is shown on, never the record itself.
`ink` and `trail` are shown on a `line`, because both are stroke-only — a path walked out and
back has no inside to fill. `mark` is shown on a `circle`, the opposite case: a shape that DOES
docs.presetsSurfaces.plate: The default look: a panel fill and a bordered edge. What a node draws when nothing else was
docs.presetsSurfaces.bare: The same fill, the stroke taken away. Reregister either name and every card wearing it changes
in one step, while neither box moves a unit — the record is the unit of restyling, not the node.
docs.presetsSurfaces.zone: The marked-out area: see-through ground, a dashed edge. The look a desk or a drop target
reaches for to say "here" rather than "this is a card".
docs.presetsSurfaces.ink: A stroke and nothing else. `ink` and `trail` are the only two stock records with no fill layer
at all — the record a walk out and back actually needs, since everything visible is the line.
docs.presetsSurfaces.trail: The same kind of run, dashed. The path did not change — the record did, and that is the whole
lesson: the pattern on a line lives in the SURFACE, never in the geometry.
